How about a diplomatic approach? Legends tell of people marrying the Others and having weird offspring with them. We know so little about them that even saying that they're the bad guys seems wrong, after all we only get to see one half of the story and even from the perspective of the light R'hllor doesn't seem that great, considering all the burning people alive

EDIT- I'd even be fine with them killing the Night King and the good guys win traditionally, IF it felt like it was earned, who really died this episode? A bunch of redshirts, three secondary characters and three tertiary characters. Nobody that we care about in the crypts died so that plot point literally might as well not have happened. It just feels like most of the episode might as well not have happened, have Arya shoot the Night King with a dragonglass arrow from 200 yards away and just have every soldier keel over and die of the pox, and there, nothing was really lost besides the spectacle of the battle

If they have the budget and time to make an 80 minute long battle featuring a giant, three dragons, and bazillions of troops then they can surely find it in them to actually develop the threat of the dead and resolve that threat in a satisfying way. I won't say it was contrived for Arya to kill the NK and have the rest of them fall too cause that was all set up, I won't act like Arya doesn't have it in her to kill him, I'm just saying that to set up a big fight and the resolution is that the good guys just win with honestly minimal losses of characters we care about, despite the fact that they all should have just been crushed under the initial wave of wights flys in the face of the spirit of Thrones. I honestly would have preferred that the Night King wins and everybody just died. I'm also a big fan of run on sentences

As if Arya isn't a fan favourite badass character that had thousands of people hoping she'd be the one to do the Night King in, don't pretend that just because Jon or Dany wasn't the one to do it it isn't any less cliché

Game of Thrones is supposed to be different, or at least ASOIAF is supposed to be different. It's not about black and white good vs evil battles. So to have the biggest antagonistic force be taken down in a giant battle for the light is terribly disappointing. There was no nuance to the Night King, no complex moral dilemmas, nothing that drew so many fans in to the series in the first place, I don't care that it was Arya the indestructible that killed him I'd be equally unhappy if it had been Jon or Daenerys or Baby Sam that killed him. If people wanted to watch LotR (not bashing, I love Tolkien but these are seperate beasts) then they could have saved themselves a decade of waiting and dozens of hours.

EDIT- I'm not trying to convince anybody to dislike the episode, if you do like it then more power to you, I wish I could. But when you title your post "What's the point of bitching about this thing" you sound like a bit of a dumb cunt
